declared_in: reports/decision.md, section "Evaluation round 3 (written Nov 15, 2026, before any item below was scored)"
git_dirty_source_means: a file under src/ or a Python file in app/ differed from git_commit
what: Year-block intervals around version 1's system-minus-rule differences. Lower is better for every quantity here (a cost, or an error in weeks), so a difference below zero favours the system.

alert.name: 4-week system cost minus Persistence
alert.rows_used: Rio Grande test rows of the 4-week alert (weekly, 2019 on)
alert.year_unit: the calendar year of the issue date (the date the forecast was made), all counties together

block1.caveat: Percentile interval from 8 resampled years (block 1). With this few years it is too narrow: in simulation a nominal 95% interval covered the truth about 88% of the time with 8 years and 92% with 18 (80% and 90% with two-year blocks), and is expected to be less if years are dependent. These coverage figures come from a simulation with independent years and a true difference of zero, not from this project's data.

block2.caveat: Percentile interval from 8 resampled years (block 2).
